# HelioFleet

> HelioFleet is a free, open-source web tool (MIT licence) by Soumyaranjan Dash (National Solar Observatory) that shows where the heliophysics spacecraft are relative to the Sun and Earth on any date since 2010, what each of them can see, and which high-resolution solar observations were made together. Positions come from JPL Horizons ephemerides, refreshed monthly. It runs in the browser; every number it shows can be downloaded or reproduced with SunPy.

This file is a guide for automated readers and search tools: where each method is described, which data files hold what, how to link to an exact view, and where code and figures come from. All pages are static and public. The interface is in English, Hindi and Spanish (`?lang=hi`, `?lang=es`); the methods and help pages are in English.

Spacecraft covered: SDO, SOHO, Aditya-L1, ACE, Wind, DSCOVR, IMAP, SOLAR-1 (SWFO-L1), Carruthers, Solar Orbiter, Parker Solar Probe, BepiColombo, STEREO-A, STEREO-B (contact lost 2014-10-01) and MAVEN (contact lost 2025-12-06), with the planets.

## Pages

- [Map](https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofleet/): positions of the fleet around the Sun and Earth for any UTC moment since 2010; spacecraft cards; Parker spirals; CME fronts from NASA DONKI; coronagraph fields of view; a solar surface map over SDO/HMI synoptic magnetograms showing what each observer sees; research tools (coordinates, viewing geometry, alignment search, spot visibility, time-series export, animation).
- [Sky view](https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofleet/sky.html): instrument fields of view projected onto the plane of the sky seen from Earth or a chosen spacecraft; MLSO K-Cor and UCoMP; "who sees this point"; observation footprints of DKIST, IRIS, Hinode/EIS and Solar Orbiter drawn over SDO/AIA 171 Å, AIA 193 Å or HMI magnetogram images; a finder for coordinated observations.
- [Methods and accuracy](https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofleet/methods.html): data sources, coordinate frames, formulas for every derived quantity, the sky-view projection, validation against JPL Horizons and SunPy, and known limits.
- [How to use](https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofleet/help.html): what every tool is for, the full list of link parameters, and worked example links.

## Linking to an exact view

Each page's address holds its whole state; a link reproduces what was on screen.

- Map: `t` (UTC, e.g. `2025-03-22T22:25Z`), `frame` (`hee` Earth-fixed or `hae` inertial), `view` (`top`, `side`), `zoom`, `trail` (days), `planets`, `spirals`, `wind` (km/s), `hide` (bodies), `cme`, `fov` (instruments), `spot` (`c,LON,LAT` Carrington or `s,LON,LAT` Stonyhurst), `tab` (`coords`, `geom`, `align`, `vis`, `series`, `anim`), `align` (`kind,a,b,tolerance,from,to`; rerun on opening), `lang`, `theme`. Sections: `#map`, `#coverage`, `#tools`.
- Sky view: `t`, `obs` (observer: `earth`, `solo`, `psp`, `bepi`, `sta`, `stb`, `maven`), `zoom` (solar radii), `fov`, `ground`, `hide`, `pt` (marked point, solar radii), `hl` (highlighted observation id), `img` (`aia171`, `aia193`, `hmi`), `oi` (instruments shown), `find` (facilities `dkist,iris,eis,solo`), `ffrom`, `fto` (YYYY-MM-DD), `fwhere` (`any`, `disk`, `limb`). Sections: `#observations`, `#finder`, `#point`, `#cryo`, `#sites`.
- Examples: [DKIST, IRIS, Hinode/EIS and Solar Orbiter on the same disk target in 2024](https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofleet/sky.html?find=dkist,iris,eis,solo&ffrom=2024-01-01&fto=2024-12-31&fwhere=disk#finder); [viewing geometry at Parker's perihelion of 22 March 2025](https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofleet/?t=2025-03-22T22:25Z&tab=geom#tools); [Solar Orbiter and Parker radial alignments in 2025](https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofleet/?t=2025-06-01T00:00Z&tab=align&align=radial,solo,psp,5,2025-01-01,2025-12-31#tools).

## Methods (summary; full text on the methods page)

- Frames: Stonyhurst heliographic (HEEQ) and Carrington longitudes from the IAU rotation model (pole RA 286.13°, Dec 63.87°; W = 84.176° + 14.1844°/day since J2000 TT), with the Sun seen one light time in the past, as in SunPy.
- Parker-spiral footpoint: φ_foot = φ + Ω (r − R☉) / v, Ω = 14.1844°/day sidereal, constant radial wind speed v.
- Visibility of a surface point from an observer at heliographic (L, B, r): μ = sin θ sin B + cos θ cos B cos(φ − L) > R☉ / r.
- Viewing geometry per observer: light time r/c and offset from Earth (r − r⊕)/c; apparent solar radius arcsin(R☉/r), R☉ = 695 700 km (as RSUN_OBS); B0 and Stonyhurst longitude (HGLT_OBS, HGLN_OBS); L0 with the observer's own light time (CRLN_OBS); one arcsecond at disk centre spans (r − R☉) tan 1″; magnification relative to Earth (r⊕ − R☉)/(r − R☉).
- Sky view: lines of sight from each instrument are followed to the plane through Sun centre perpendicular to the Sun–observer line.
- Observation footprints are drawn with the pointing recorded with each observation. Solar Orbiter fields are carried into Earth's view through the solar surface (off the disk, at the point of closest approach to Sun centre). Coordinated observations are groups of observations by different facilities that overlap in time and whose fields overlap in Earth's view; durations over 24 hours are treated as faulty catalogue entries and cut to a day.
- Accuracy: Stonyhurst and Carrington coordinates agree with SunPy to 0.0004° (worst 0.005°); see the validation table on the methods page.

## Data files (JSON unless noted; refreshed on the 1st of each month)

- [data/manifest.json](https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofleet/data/manifest.json): each body's time span, sample step (days), units and available years; the timeline; last and next update.
- `data/<body>/<year>.json` (e.g. [data/psp/2025.json](https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofleet/data/psp/2025.json)): `t0` (Julian date, UT), `step` (days), `n`, `d` = flat x, y, z array; heliocentric J2000 ecliptic in au, or geocentric in km for `*_geo` (L1 monitors).
- [data/events.json](https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofleet/data/events.json): DONKI flares, CMEs and geomagnetic storms.
- [data/upcoming.json](https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofleet/data/upcoming.json) and [calendar.ics](https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofleet/calendar.ics): upcoming perihelia, alignments, quadratures, conjunctions and eclipses.
- [data/synoptic/index.json](https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofleet/data/synoptic/index.json): SDO/HMI radial-field synoptic maps by Carrington rotation; each `crNNNN.png` is 360 × 180, 8-bit, uniform in Carrington longitude and sine latitude, 0 = no data, 1–255 = −20 to +20 G.
- [data/ground/cryonirsp.json](https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofleet/data/ground/cryonirsp.json): DKIST Cryo-NIRSP datasets (id, times, waveband, mode, proposal, footprint polygon in helioprojective arcsec).
- [data/obs/index.json](https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofleet/data/obs/index.json) and `data/obs/YYYY-MM.json`: observation footprints of IRIS, Hinode/EIS, DKIST (VBI, ViSP, DL-NIRSP, VTF) and Solar Orbiter (EUI-HRI, PHI-HRT, SPICE). Row fields: `i` instrument, `t0`, `t1` (UTC), `f` frame (`E` Earth view, `S` Solar Orbiter view), `x`, `y` closed polygon (arcsec), `o` Solar Orbiter position (Stonyhurst lon, lat in degrees, distance in au), `id`, `n` description, `u` data link; IRIS rows add `sx`, `sy` (slit-jaw field).
- [data/obs/coordinated.json](https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofleet/data/obs/coordinated.json): coordinated groups; columns `start`, `hours`, `x`, `y`, `r_over_rsun`, `facilities` (e.g. `dkist+iris+solo`), `observations` (counts per instrument), `open` (observation to open), `open_mid`.
- [data/ground/context/index.json](https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofleet/data/ground/context/index.json): archived SDO/AIA 171 Å, 193 Å and HMI cutouts for each Cryo-NIRSP run, full disk (`<key>_<channel>_disk.jpg`) and zoomed (`<key>_<channel>.jpg`), with centre, scale (arcsec/pixel), image time and the pointing correction applied (`shift`, arcsec).

## Code

- Source: [github.com/sr-dash/heliofleet](https://github.com/sr-dash/heliofleet). Data scripts use the Python standard library unless noted.
- [scripts/fetch_ephemeris.py](https://github.com/sr-dash/heliofleet/blob/main/scripts/fetch_ephemeris.py): JPL Horizons vectors to `data/<body>/`.
- [scripts/fetch_observations.py](https://github.com/sr-dash/heliofleet/blob/main/scripts/fetch_observations.py): IRIS (LMSAL HCR), Hinode/EIS (as-run catalogue), DKIST (Data Center API) and Solar Orbiter (SOAR) footprints, and the coordinated groups.
- [scripts/fetch_context.py](https://github.com/sr-dash/heliofleet/blob/main/scripts/fetch_context.py): Helioviewer cutouts for Cryo-NIRSP runs with a limb-fit pointing check (Pillow, NumPy).
- [scripts/fetch_synoptic.py](https://github.com/sr-dash/heliofleet/blob/main/scripts/fetch_synoptic.py): HMI synoptic maps from JSOC. [scripts/fetch_events.py](https://github.com/sr-dash/heliofleet/blob/main/scripts/fetch_events.py): DONKI events. [scripts/make_reference.py](https://github.com/sr-dash/heliofleet/blob/main/scripts/make_reference.py) and [tests/validate.mjs](https://github.com/sr-dash/heliofleet/blob/main/tests/validate.mjs): the Horizons and SunPy cross-check.
- In the page: the Coordinates and Viewing geometry tabs give CSV, JSON and a SunPy script that recomputes the table from JPL Horizons; the observations panel gives Footprints (CSV) and a SunPy script that fetches the AIA or HMI image from JSOC through Fido, draws the footprints and saves the figure as PDF.
- Minimal SunPy example (Stonyhurst and own-light-time Carrington coordinates of an observer):

```python
from astropy.time import Time
from sunpy.coordinates import frames, get_horizons_coord
t = Time("2025-03-22T22:25:00")
psp = get_horizons_coord("Parker Solar Probe", t).transform_to(frames.HeliographicStonyhurst(obstime=t))
l0 = psp.transform_to(frames.HeliographicCarrington(obstime=t, observer=psp)).lon
print(psp.radius.to("AU"), psp.lon, psp.lat, l0)
```

## Figures

- [assets/og-image.png](https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofleet/assets/og-image.png): the map during the total solar eclipse of 8 April 2024 (1200 × 630).
- [assets/og-sky.jpg](https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofleet/assets/og-sky.jpg): the sky view on 16 October 2023, DKIST, IRIS, Hinode/EIS and Solar Orbiter footprints over SDO/AIA 171 Å with a zoomed inset (1200 × 630).
- The map and the sky view save PNG and PDF snapshots with a key of every layer; the map also records MP4 or GIF animations. Archived Cryo-NIRSP runs save as PNG with a caption; other observation figures are made with the SunPy script above from JSOC FITS.
- SDO images in the sky view come from Helioviewer (SDO/AIA and SDO/HMI, courtesy of NASA/SDO and the AIA and HMI science teams).
